transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-22
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Li (Redwood SE), Ethan Morales (Astral - Head of Partnerships), Priya Kapoor (Astral - Sales Director), Liam O'Connor (Astral - Solutions Architect)

Summary:
Quick pipeline sync to align on co-sell motions, handoff process, top target accounts, margin expectations, and to scope a short pilot/benchmark. Action items and next steps agreed at end.

Topics:
- Current Astral pipeline and priority accounts
- Joint GTM and deal registration
- Technical gating (benchmarks, security)
- Commissioning / margin split and referral fees
- Pilot scope and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Jordan from Redwood here, with Maya on the line. How are you all doing?
[00:06] Ethan (Astral): Good, good thanks. Busy but excited to dig in.
[00:09] Priya (Astral): Hi all. Great to meet you, Maya.
[00:11] Maya (Redwood): Hi Priya, hi Ethan, Liam—thanks for having us.
[00:15] Jordan: Quick agenda — we wanted to run through your top co-sell targets, talk through what triggers a joint outreach versus referral, go over security / pilot ask, and then close with next steps. Sound OK?
[00:24] Priya: Yup, perfect. We have about six deals we think are co-sell-ready, three of which are top priority.
[00:30] Ethan: Right, the three are finance sector customers where latency is a big ask, plus one telco and two retail.
[00:36] Jordan: Great. On Redwood side we typically recommend either a hosted integration for fast time-to-value or dedicated capacity for higher SLA/throughput customers. For the finance ones I suspect Dedicated or Private will be in scope because of compliance.
[00:46] Liam: Yeah, most likely dedicated or VPC — data residency and KMS are big for them. We should confirm Redwood's KMS/HSM options — last time we saw the doc it mentioned KMS integrations but wanted to double-check.
[00:59] Maya: We do support KMS and HSM integrations for our Private deployments, and Dedicated can be configured with customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations. I'll share the security pack after the call — there's a SOC 2 and architecture diagram too.
[01:12] Ethan: Perfect. Can you also confirm SAML or SSO for the console access? Some of our ops teams require that for co-managed dashboards.
[01:20] Jordan: Yes SAML SSO is supported for the Console and RBAC can be tied to your IDP. We'll include those bits in the security sheet.
[01:26] Priya: On the commercial side, what's the typical commission split for co-sell? We heard some partners ran into low margins with other vendors.
[01:33] Jordan: We generally do a tiered model — referral fee for simple leads, escalate to a co-sell commission when Redwood is taking on the majority of the integration/configuration work. Typical ranges we've seen are 10-20% for referrals and up to 25-30% for full co-sell depending on committed ARR and contract length. We'll share a sample matrix.
[01:47] Ethan: Ok that's in the ballpark. We'll need something explicit for our finance team to sign off.
[01:52] Jordan: Agreed, we can send an example commission matrix and a co-sell agreement template.
[01:56] Maya: On the technical gating — for the pilot we should define success metrics: latency p99, cost per 1k tokens, and throughput targets. We'll run a 2-week benchmark against 2-3 sample prompts from Astral.
[02:08] Liam: Good. Our apps have a mix of long context and short responses. We can provide representative prompt sets, but note that the KV cache pattern is important for the retail use case.
[02:17] Maya: Noted — we sometimes see the transcript tool transcribe KV cache as "K V cash," so apologies if the doc is weird — but yes KV cache and prefix caching are big help. We'll include batching and quantization profiles in the benchmark.
[02:29] Priya: Timeline-wise we want to get the pilot running in November if possible.
[02:33] Jordan: That lines up. If we get account intros and the sample prompts by the end of next week, Maya can start the benchmarks in the first week of November.
[02:41] Ethan: One operational question — how will leads be registered? We need a clear deal registration to avoid conflict with other partners.
[02:48] Jordan: We have a deal registration flow in the partner portal. For joint co-sell opportunities, we recommend registering early and adding the expected ARR and stage. We can also set up a shared spreadsheet for the initial pipeline so your sales ops can map contacts.
[02:59] Priya: We'll want a short form to capture who owns outreach, who's doing solutioning, and the commission type.
[03:06] Jordan: Makes sense — we can provide a template that includes those fields.
[03:10] Liam: On the security checklist — our legal will want to see audit logs and retention policies. Does Redwood provide per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdowns?
[03:19] Maya: Yes, our Console offers token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards and tracing. We'll include examples. For audit logs and retention we can work with your security team on retention windows and export.
[03:30] Ethan: That addresses a lot, thanks. Any competitive concerns? Some of our targets mentioned running pilots with CloudAI and Nimbus Labs.
[03:38] Jordan: Totally — the differentiator for us is production-grade inference and unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private, plus the cost-aware controls. We also support graceful fallbacks if capacity is constrained which is handy for big retailers.
[03:51] Priya: Regarding go-to-market — we'd like a joint deck for sales reps and a 1-pager for executive sponsors. Can Redwood help with a co-branded deck?
[03:59] Jordan: Absolutely, we have a co-sell playbook and a starter deck. We'll tailor it to the verticals you mentioned (finance, telco, retail).
[04:06] Maya: I'll add a slide on the pilot scope and the benchmark methodology so reps know what to expect.
[04:11] Ethan: For the finance customers we should ensure we call out Private deploy and on-prem options — some of them are air-gapped or have strict residency requirements.
[04:18] Jordan: Noted. We can include a Private deployment slide with KMS, HSM, and audit controls.
[04:23] Priya: A quick pricing question — do you have any partner enablement discounts or demo credits we can use during discovery?
[04:30] Jordan: We can offer demo credits for initial pilots and a partner enablement discount for the first committed quarter for deals that register as co-sell. I'll confirm numbers in the agreement we send.
[04:40] Liam: When you run the benchmarks, can you include both 8k and 32k context tests? Our telco customer likely needs longer sequences.
[04:46] Maya: Yes we'll include both, and we'll test different quantization settings so we can provide latency vs cost tradeoffs.
[04:54] Ethan: For account contacts, we typically have 2 internal champions per deal. We'll share those in the list.
[04:59] Jordan: Great. Last piece — handoff cadence. How do you want to run co-sell? Weekly sync? Bi-weekly?
[05:05] Priya: Weekly during pilot, then bi-weekly during rollout.
[05:09] Jordan: Works for us. We'll set up an initial weekly call through the pilot.
[05:12] Ethan: Sounds good.
[05:14] [10:00 mark slight cross-talk about calendar scheduling—inaudible]
[05:35] Jordan: I want to flag one possible blocker — some deals may want SLA-backed latency and uptime. For those we need to move to Dedicated with an SLA contract. That adds procurement time.
[05:46] Priya: Noted. We'll flag which accounts need an SLA.
[05:50] Maya: Also, for the telco customer, we'll want to validate throughput at scale. We might need burst capacity configured.
[05:58] Jordan: Right — our Dedicated product supports configurable autoscaling and burst. We'll document the typical scaling profile.
[06:04] Ethan: On the legal side, what about data residency clauses? Some of our customers require EU-only storage.
[06:11] Jordan: We have region-specific hosting and can lock to EU regions for data residency. For Private deployments we can do on-prem as well.
[06:18] Priya: Ok good. Anything else we should track?
[06:21] Jordan: I'll send the co-sell agreement, commission matrix, and the partner portal access link. Maya will send the benchmark plan and security pack. Astral will send the account list and draft outreach template.
[06:32] Liam: We'll also include a short tech notes doc for the Solutions Architect who will own the pilot.
[06:37] Ethan: Thanks, folks. One more ask — can Redwood share a recent case study with similar finance customer outcomes (latency reduction and cost per token improvements)?
[06:47] Jordan: Yes, we'll include a one-pager case study.
[06:50] Priya: Cool. That covers it from our side.
[06:53] Jordan: Great. We'll follow up with the artifacts and get the next meeting scheduled for the week of Nov 2. Appreciate your time.
[06:59] Ethan: Thanks everyone.
[07:01] Maya: Thanks all. Bye.

Recap / Agreed next steps:
- Jordan to send co-sell agreement, commission matrix, partner portal link, and co-branded starter deck (by 2026-10-25).
- Maya to run the performance/cost benchmark across 8k and 32k contexts and share results (by 2026-11-03).
- Astral (Ethan/Priya) to share top accounts, champions, and outreach template (by 2026-10-29).
- Schedule weekly pilot sync during the pilot, starting week of 2026-11-02.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attribution and minor word swaps, but overall captures action items and technical asks.
